checks.invariant: OAuth callback must bind the authorization code to the initiating owner session, not only a bearer state JWT
checks.result: GET /integrations/facebook/oauth/callback has no get_current_user dependency. complete_oauth decodes HS256 state, loads that account/user, and writes sealed user and Page tokens. test_oauth_callback_stores_encrypted_page_token issues the callback with only code and state.

checks.invariant: OAuth state JWT must bind aud, iss, jti/one-time use, and PKCE; staff JWTs must not satisfy the callback
checks.result: encode_oauth_state emits purpose, account_id, user_id, iat, exp only. decode_oauth_state verifies HS256 and exp, sets verify_aud False, and does not check aud, iss, or jti and does not consume state. oauth_dialog_url has no code_challenge. Staff JWTs lack purpose=meta_oauth so they fail the purpose check; the same SECRET_KEY signs both token types.

checks.invariant: Meta redirect_uri and post-callback Location must not be taken from Host or forwarded headers
checks.result: meta_oauth_redirect_uri uses META_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI or a localhost default. public_web_origin uses PUBLIC_WEB_ORIGIN, else the first CORS_ORIGINS entry, else the first cors_allow_origins value. Neither reads request Host or X-Forwarded-*.

checks.invariant: Page and user access tokens must not be returned in API bodies, redirects, or connect logs
checks.result: FacebookStatusOut and listed_pages expose page id/name/user id only. complete_oauth redirects to /account?facebook=… with no token query. OAuth failure logs account_id and the Graph error string, not the access token. oauth/start is owner-gated; complete_oauth rejects a non-owner user_id from state.

checks.invariant: Catalogger and client must receive 403 on Facebook connect, preview, publish, Approve, Post now, and settings
checks.result: require_facebook_poster calls can_manage_integrations, which is owner-only. Tests assert catalogger 403 on oauth/start, preview, POST /facebook/posts, calendar cancel, and calendar Approve/Post now. Clients are blocked by enforce_client_http. GET /facebook/posts and GET status are authenticated but not owner-gated.

checks.invariant: HTTP publish and calendar Approve/Post now must not send Graph posts unless confirm is true; force must not drop the owner or confirm gate
checks.result: FacebookPublishIn and FacebookCalendarApproveIn default confirm to false. publish_posts raises 400 when confirm is false. force only skips the already-posted/scheduled guard and still requires confirm plus require_facebook_poster on the HTTP routes.

checks.invariant: calendar_auto_approve must not let a non-owner reach publish_posts or skip the confirm gate
checks.result: sync_facebook_calendar_after_snapshot, when facebook_calendar_auto_approve is set, loads the first owner and calls publish_posts or start_facebook_posts_in_background with confirm=True. apply_engagement_snapshot always invokes that sync. POST /integrations/engagement/snapshots is get_current_user only, so a catalogger ingest publishes as the synthetic owner. PATCH settings is owner-gated but also syncs every sale immediately when the flag is turned on. Background _run_facebook_posts does not re-check require_facebook_poster.

checks.invariant: Ordinary CSRF requires ambient cookies on publish/Approve/Post now
checks.result: Those mutations use OAuth2PasswordBearer get_current_user. The dashboard sends Authorization Bearer from localStorage and does not attach a session cookie. Ordinary CSRF does not apply to this ambient-credential shape.

checks.invariant: Facebook secrets at rest must use authenticated encryption and must not fall open to XOR when cryptography is missing
checks.result: seal_facebook_secret uses Fernet when import succeeds. On ImportError it stores xor: plus a repeating XOR of sha256(meta-page:SECRET_KEY), ignoring META_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY. unseal_facebook_secret always accepts the xor: prefix even when Fernet is installed. requirements.txt pins cryptography>=42.0.0 and both Dockerfiles pip-install it; a missing or broken import still takes the XOR branch.

checks.invariant: CT Seller secrets share the same ImportError XOR fail-open
checks.result: ctseller.seal_secret uses the same try/Fernet except/XOR pattern. CT XOR key is sha256(SECRET_KEY) with no ctseller: prefix, while Fernet uses sha256(ctseller:SECRET_KEY).

checks.invariant: Unsealed Page or user tokens must not appear in API responses or connect logs
checks.result: connection_status unseals the Page token only to compute a boolean connected flag and does not put the secret on FacebookStatusOut. listed_pages drops Graph access_token fields. The OAuth callback test asserts the live Page token is absent from the stored ciphertext.

candidates.title: Unauthenticated Facebook OAuth callback writes Page tokens from HS256 state alone
candidates.description: GET /integrations/facebook/oauth/callback is unauthenticated. A 15-minute HS256 JWT signed with SECRET_KEY (purpose=meta_oauth, account_id, user_id, exp; no aud, iss, or jti) is enough to exchange a Facebook code and persist user and Page access tokens on the account named in state. There is no PKCE verifier, no one-time state store, and no check that the browser is the owner who called /oauth/start. A signed start URL is therefore a transferable capability: a Facebook admin who completes an attacker-started dialog binds their Page tokens to the attacker tenant, and a stolen owner start URL lets another Facebook user overwrite that tenant's stored Page connection. Staff JWTs are not accepted as state because they lack purpose=meta_oauth. Meta redirect_uri is taken from settings, not Host.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: The callback trusts only decode_oauth_state on a SECRET_KEY HS256 JWT and then complete_oauth writes sealed Facebook tokens without session binding, PKCE, audience, or single-use state.

trace.description: Unauthenticated GET receives Facebook code and state and calls complete_oauth.
jwt.decode verifies HS256 and exp with verify_aud False; only purpose, account_id, and user_id are checked.
State account/user are loaded; is_owner is required, but no current Bearer or cookie is required.
Facebook user and Page tokens are sealed onto the state-selected account and committed.

evidence.description: State claims are purpose, account_id, user_id, iat, exp; no aud, iss, jti, or nonce.
decode options require exp and disable audience verification.
oauth_dialog_url sends code flow without code_challenge.
Staff access tokens use the same SECRET_KEY and also set verify_aud False, but omit purpose.
Unit test completes OAuth and stores a Page token using only code and state.

blockers: No OS-enforced sandbox and no parent scratch-promotion procedure, so target code was not executed.
Facebook authorization-code single-use, consent-screen behavior, and the deployed Meta Valid OAuth Redirect URIs list are not observable from source.

candidates.title: Catalogger snapshot ingest publishes to the Page when calendar_auto_approve is on
candidates.description: HTTP preview, publish, Approve, and Post now call require_facebook_poster and publish_posts refuses confirm=false. force does not drop those gates. A parallel path does: if the owner has set facebook_calendar_auto_approve, sync_facebook_calendar_after_snapshot selects the first owner user and calls publish_posts or the in-memory poster thread with confirm=True. POST /integrations/engagement/snapshots is available to any authenticated account member and always runs that sync, so a catalogger can choose Push items in a snapshot and cause Page schedule/publish without the owner confirm click. PATCH /integrations/facebook/settings is owner-only but also syncs every engagement sale as soon as the flag is enabled.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: calendar_auto_approve hard-codes confirm=True as a synthetic owner and is triggered by catalogger-reachable snapshot ingest, bypassing require_facebook_poster on the publish routes.

trace.description: Any authenticated account member can POST a watcher snapshot; there is no owner gate.
After commit, every snapshot calls sync_facebook_calendar_after_snapshot.
When facebook_calendar_auto_approve is true, the first owner is loaded and pending slots are published with confirm=True.
create_page_feed_post runs under the synthetic owner without a new HTTP confirm from that owner.

evidence.description: can_manage_integrations is owner-only; that is the HTTP Facebook poster gate.
publish_posts returns 400 unless confirm is true.
Auto-approve passes confirm=True into the background poster.
Enabling the setting immediately syncs every engagement sale.
The background runner does not call require_facebook_poster before publish_posts.
Turning calendar_auto_approve on causes Graph feed calls without a per-slot confirm body.

blockers: No OS-enforced sandbox, so the catalogger-snapshot plus auto-approve path was not executed.
Whether the deployed watcher/extension uses a catalogger token for POST /integrations/engagement/snapshots is not source-provable.

validation_plan.local: Using the existing TestClient fixtures, connect a Page, set calendar_auto_approve as owner, then authenticate as a catalogger and POST /integrations/engagement/snapshots for a future Push lot with Graph feed mocked. Expect create_page_feed_post to run and a scheduled FacebookPagePost row to appear. Repeat with the flag false and expect no feed call.

candidates.title: Facebook and CT Seller sealing fall open to SECRET_KEY XOR when Fernet import fails
candidates.description: seal_facebook_secret intends Fernet with a key derived from META_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY or SECRET_KEY. If cryptography cannot be imported, it writes xor: plus a repeating XOR of sha256(meta-page:SECRET_KEY), ignoring META_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY. unseal_facebook_secret always decrypts xor: blobs with that SECRET_KEY material even when Fernet is available. ctseller.seal_secret has the same ImportError fallback; its XOR key is sha256(SECRET_KEY) without the ctseller: prefix used by Fernet. Dockerfiles install cryptography>=42.0.0, so the branch is a fail-open for a missing or broken import rather than the default image path. API schemas do not return unsealed tokens.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Token seal functions catch ImportError and persist unauthenticated XOR under a xor: prefix keyed from SECRET_KEY, and unseal accepts that prefix unconditionally.

trace.description: Fresh Facebook user and Page tokens are passed to seal_facebook_secret before commit.
Fernet is attempted with sha256(meta-page: dedicated-or-SECRET_KEY).
ImportError stores xor: ciphertext derived only from SECRET_KEY.

evidence.description: Fernet key uses META_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY when set; XOR does not.
unseal always handles xor: with SECRET_KEY material.
CT Seller secrets use the same ImportError XOR fallback.
Comments document optional META_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY with SECRET_KEY derivation.
API image pip-installs requirements.txt, including cryptography.

blockers: No OS-enforced sandbox, so ImportError was not forced at runtime.
Whether every deployed process (Railway API, worker, and any non-Docker host) can import cryptography is not source-provable.

validation_plan.local: Monkeypatch cryptography.fernet import to raise ImportError, call seal_facebook_secret and ctseller.seal_secret with dummy strings, assert xor: prefixes, then unseal and compare. Set META_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY to a distinct dummy and assert Facebook XOR still follows SECRET_KEY. Restore the import and assert Fernet output has no xor: prefix.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner runs a one-shot import cryptography check in the production API and worker images and confirms no xor: rows exist on accounts.facebook_*_enc or CT Seller secret columns.
